summary: Iter 14 — tested Deal-Of-The-Night scheduling, Auto-Close, Merge, Move-line on backend (6/6 pytest passing) and QuickBar + Combo Schedule editor + Auto-Close btn + Seat cycle on frontend. Backend all green. Frontend: QuickBar 3-tile flow + cash payment + receipt modal works. Combo schedule fields render (Mon..Sun/start/end). Auto-Close button on Floorplan clickable. FOUND: seat cycle skips seats in dev/StrictMode due to state mutation in cycleSeat.

ui_bugs.issue: Seat cycle skips values in React.StrictMode because updater mutates lines[i] directly (lines[i].seat = ...). StrictMode invokes the updater twice with the same reference, so the mutation compounds: e.g. guests=4 produced S1->S3->S1->S3 instead of S1->S2->S3->S4->S1. In production build it will not skip (StrictMode double-invoke is dev-only), but the updater is impure and should be fixed for correctness.
ui_bugs.fix_hint: Replace lines[i].seat = ... with lines[i] = { ...lines[i], seat: (cur % guests) + 1 } so the updater is a pure function of its input.

action_items: Fix cycleSeat impurity in CartTicket.jsx (mutation inside setOrder updater). Use immutable line copy so React.StrictMode double-invoke does not double-cycle the seat.

routers/orders.py auto_close endpoint: recomputes revenue as sum of order totals, records payment.auto_closed=True, and frees tables to 'dirty' — matches spec. Guarded to admin/manager only.

CartTicket.cycleSeat mutates state (bug — see ui_bugs). Same pattern check should be applied to any other setOrder updaters — a quick grep is warranted.
ComboEditor: schedule fields render only when combo-schedule-toggle is on; time inputs use native <input type='time'> which is fine.
QuickBar.jsx: cash/card flow POSTs order, fires, then pays and shows Receipt — verified end-to-end (subtotal HK$404.8 for 3 cocktails; receipt rendered).

rca_of_the_issue: Seat cycle skip (S1->S3): React.StrictMode intentionally invokes state-updater functions twice in dev to surface impurities. CartTicket.cycleSeat does `lines[i].seat = (cur % guests) + 1`, mutating the same line object from o.lines. The two updater calls share the same object reference so the second call sees the already-cycled value and cycles again. Reproduce: set guests=N (>=3), click line-seat-0 once, observe seat increases by 2 instead of 1. Fix by replacing the object mutation with `lines[i] = { ...lines[i], seat: (cur % guests) + 1 }` (or use functional immutable update).
